correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for every a>b>0 and every t∈[0,b] via the precise disk-support intersection, a support-convexification argument at θ_t, support-area and perimeter integrals, and a Taylor expansion with the cancellation γ/5−β=2α/15. The 7/2 coefficient 16α^(−3/2)/105 follows from integrating the first-variation perimeter correction. The analytic argument handles t=t_* and t=b by continuity and states a separate disk case. A standalone checker uses high-precision integration and an independent half-space intersection, with several post-threshold cases and coefficient convergence. Computation is diagnostic only.

value.rationale: This is a motivated, exact geometry probability law for a canonical convex body. It identifies the first breakdown of a familiar inner Steiner quadratic, gives its non-integer singularity with a sharp strictly positive coefficient and classifies the changed boundary geometry. The same full distribution recovers the ellipse semiaxes; this is structural information, not a one-off numeric evaluation. General clearance and morphology questions make this invariant and threshold natural.
